title: LLM ingest turnstile: format normalizer and staged certification pipeline
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: we receive heterogeneous community LLM checkpoints with varied formats (torch .pt/.bin, safetensors, legacy HF sharded checkpoints, gguf, tarball bundles). Current intake is brittle: conversion failures surface late, profiler runs against wrong shard schemes, and pins are recommended without systematic performance evidence.

Goal: build an end-to-end 'ingest turnstile' that deterministically normalizes incoming artifacts into a canonical runtime artifact, performs staged validation and performance profiling across representative infra, and publishes a vetted pin + performance profile to the model catalog automatically or with gated approval.

Scope: weights intake adapters, format normalizer, deterministic hashing & provenance, staged certification (smoke -> functional -> perf), automatic pin recommendation + human approval workflow, and profile publishing. Support optional quantization/gguf conversion paths but keep conversion idempotent and reversible (retain original artifact).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Ingest adapter accepts common formats and emits canonical artifact with provenance metadata (source URL, uploader, signature/hash).
- Automated smoke tests (load, sample generation) pass in CI for 95% of community-provided checkpoint variants within pipeline SLA (5m per artifact).
- Performance profile (latency p50/p95, memory peak, throughput at 1/4/1/4 concurrency, token cost estimate) is generated and attached to the catalog entry.
- Pin recommendation algorithm outputs a suggested pin string plus confidence score; manual approval gate available.
- Rollback/canary plan defined and exercised with a staged 10% -> 50% -> 100% publish flow.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
1) Canonical artifact format: choose GGUF-first normalization with optional runtime-optimized serialized bundles. We prefer GGUF for single-file determinism and fast mmap loading; fallback to sharded safetensors when conversion fails. Trade-off: GGUF conversion can be lossy for some custom ops; those cases are surfaced to an exceptions registry for manual handling.

2) Deterministic conversion pipeline: conversions run in a hermetic container with pinned toolchain and produce an immutable artifact plus provenance manifest (SHA256 of inputs, conversion-tool-version, conversion-params). This enables reproducible rebuilds and easier debugging at customer support.

3) Perf profiling strategy: sample a small but representative prompt set (per-model family) and run on two representative hardware profiles (A100-40GB equivalent and T4-like). We'll capture latency p50/p95, memory high-water mark, and SSR (successful sample rate). We accept some sampling error in exchange for faster end-to-end throughput of onboarding. If a model shows high variance, the pipeline triggers a deeper profiling job.

4) Pin recommendation heuristics: prefer semantic pinning by family and minor-variant (eg my-llm@v1.3.0-gguf) with confidence score derived from combined validation and perf metrics. For ambiguous pins we require PM sign-off.

Operational notes: 
- Failures are classified as transient (retryable), conversion-critical (requires engineering owner), or unsupported (manual intake).
- All artifacts and manifests stored in S3 with KMS encryption and retention policy per security requirements.
- Must integrate with intake signer service for community uploads (we already have an onboarding-uploads bucket and signed-url flow).

Runbook for conversion-critical failures: 
1) Pipeline marks artifact state=needs-attention and notifies #ingest-alerts.
2) Auto-collect logs and conversion container snapshot.
3) Create triage ticket with prefilled metadata and assign to on-call ingestion engineer.

Telemetry & observability: 
- Expose per-artifact metrics: conversion duration, disk footprint, smoke-test pass/fail, perf p95.
- Dashboard: model-catalog staging tab with pending pins and their confidence score.
- Alerts: conversion duration > 30m, perf job failure rate > 5% in a 24h window.

Security & compliance: 
- Verify upload signatures when present (GPG/PKI) and capture uploader identity.
- Run a lightweight license/compliance scan against model metadata and raise a human review for non-OSI licenses.

Next steps / Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: finalize canonical format decisions, collect conversion toolchain versions, draft manifest schema (Aisha + Marco).
- Week 2: implement format adapters for safetensors, sharded HF, gguf; add unit tests and local CLI (Marco).
- Week 3: wire deterministic conversion container and provenance manifest; begin CI smoke-run integration (Marco, QA).
- Week 4: perf profiling harness + representative prompt sets + perf aggregation service hookup (PerfEng).
- Week 5: pin recommendation service + approval gate + catalog publish API (PM + Eng).

Rolling criteria to move to Done: automated onboarding for 90% of recent community submissions and PM sign-off on publish workflow and runbooks.
